expanded.discovery: Strictly speaking hCG is a glycoprotein heterodimer hormone, not a single-chain peptide, so taxonomy.is_peptide is false. It is included as a Peptocopeia candidate because PeptideTracker carries it and the peptide-research community routinely treats hCG as peptide-adjacent (LH/CG-receptor agonism, post-cycle therapy use, fertility protocols).
expanded.humanEvidence: hCG has decades of regulatory and clinical evidence. FDA-approved urinary preparations (Pregnyl, Novarel) and the recombinant choriogonadotropin alfa (Ovidrel) are indicated for induction of ovulation, final follicular maturation in assisted reproduction, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in males, and prepubertal cryptorchidism. In men with secondary hypogonadism, hCG raises intratesticular testosterone, restores serum testosterone, and is used to preserve or restore spermatogenesis when given alone or with FSH. Pediatric cryptorchidism protocols use multi-week courses to induce testicular descent, though responses are often incomplete and orchiopexy is frequently still required.
expanded.animalEvidence: Animal models established the LH-like activity of hCG on Leydig cells and corpus luteum decades ago and are now mainly used to study LHCGR signaling, placental biology, and downstream steroidogenic enzyme regulation rather than as primary efficacy data; the human evidence base is the practical reference.
expanded.mechanismDetail: hCG and LH share the LHCGR; hCG has a longer half-life due to its sialylated, more heavily glycosylated beta subunit and C-terminal peptide extension. Receptor binding activates Gs-coupled signaling, raising cAMP and activating PKA, which upregulates steroidogenic acute regulatory protein (StAR) and the steroidogenic enzyme cascade (CYP11A1, CYP17A1, HSD3B2) to convert cholesterol to androgens (Leydig cells) or progesterone (corpus luteum). Cross-talk through ERK1/2 also modulates ovarian and testicular cell proliferation.
expanded.safetyDetail: Boxed-style warnings on FDA labels include risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), arterial and venous thromboembolism, and multiple gestation when used for ovulation induction. Anaphylaxis has been reported with urinary-derived products. In male hypogonadism use, supraphysiologic dosing can cause gynecomastia and elevated estradiol; in pediatric cryptorchidism, precocious puberty can occur and therapy is stopped if it does. hCG is not approved for weight loss; FDA has issued warnings against homeopathic hCG weight-loss products.

expanded.discovery: MK-677 is a non-peptide small molecule (a spiropiperidine) that mimics ghrelin at GHSR1a, so taxonomy.is_peptide is false. Included as a Peptocopeia candidate following the HCG pattern: PeptideTracker covers it and community usage treats it as peptide-adjacent because of its overlap with peptide GH secretagogues (GHRP-2, GHRP-6, ipamorelin) and its use in growth-hormone-axis protocols.
expanded.humanEvidence: MK-677 has the largest clinical dataset of any oral GH secretagogue. The Nass et al. 2008 randomized controlled trial (Annals of Internal Medicine, n=65 healthy adults aged 60-81) showed that 25 mg/day for 12 months restored GH and IGF-1 to a young-adult range and significantly increased fat-free mass by ~1.6 kg without improving strength or function. Sevigny et al. 2008 (Neurology, n=563 mild-to-moderate Alzheimer disease patients) showed a 60-73% IGF-1 rise but no clinical benefit on cognition or function. Adunsky et al. 2011 (Phase IIb hip fracture trial, n=123) was terminated early due to a congestive heart failure signal (4/62 vs 1/61 placebo). MK-677 has never received FDA approval.
expanded.animalEvidence: Preclinical work from Merck in the 1990s established MK-677 as a potent GHSR1a agonist that elevates GH, IGF-1, and ACTH/cortisol in dogs and rats and recapitulates ghrelin-like food-intake and adiposity effects.
expanded.mechanismDetail: MK-677 binds GHSR1a (the ghrelin receptor), a Gq/11-coupled GPCR expressed on hypothalamic arcuate neurons and anterior pituitary somatotrophs. Receptor activation triggers PLC, IP3, DAG, intracellular Ca2+ mobilization, and PKC activation, leading to GHRH-like stimulation of GH release. GH then drives hepatic IGF-1 production via JAK2/STAT5. Unlike GHRH analogs, MK-677 also activates appetite-regulating NPY/AgRP circuits, explaining its hyperphagic effect.
expanded.safetyDetail: Across trials, the most consistent adverse signals are increased appetite, mild-to-moderate edema, transient cortisol elevation, and worsening insulin sensitivity / elevated fasting glucose. The Adunsky 2011 Phase IIb hip-fracture trial was terminated early after flagging a congestive heart failure imbalance (6.5% MK-677 vs 1.7% placebo, 4 of 62 vs 1 of 61), plausibly linked to GH-mediated fluid retention in patients with subclinical cardiac dysfunction. The trial cohort was frail elderly patients (mean age ~80) with high baseline cardiovascular risk, so the absolute CHF risk in younger, healthier community users is not characterized; nevertheless this signal is treated as a tile-level warning because no offsetting cardiovascular safety data exist in any other population. MK-677 is on the WADA Prohibited List as a GH secretagogue. It has no FDA approval and no formal long-term safety database in healthy populations.

Included as a Peptocopeia candidate following the HCG pattern: PeptideTracker covers it and the community treats it as peptide-adjacent because of the overlap with metabolic / longevity peptide stacks (e.g. with retatrutide, tirzepatide, BPC-157 protocols). expanded.humanEvidence: There is essentially no peer-reviewed human efficacy or safety data for 5-Amino-1MQ. It is sold by research-chemical vendors and used off-label by consumers, but no completed Phase 1 / Phase 2 trial has been published. Any human-use claims should be treated as anecdotal and outside Peptocopeia's evidence threshold; this should be flagged on the tile.
expanded.animalEvidence: Neelakantan et al. 2018 (Biochemical Pharmacology) established 5-Amino-1MQ as a selective, membrane-permeable NNMT inhibitor and showed that 20 mg/kg/day SC reversed high-fat-diet-induced obesity in mice, decreased adipocyte size and white adipose mass, and lowered plasma cholesterol without affecting food intake. Kannt et al. 2018 reported parallel results with structurally related NNMT inhibitors. Dimet-Wiley et al. 2024 (Scientific Reports) treated 22-month-old female mice with 5-Amino-1MQ 10 mg/kg/day SC for 8 weeks; the inhibitor alone increased grip strength roughly 25% in sedentary aged mice and roughly 60% combined with weighted-wheel running, supporting an aged-muscle benefit. Additional preclinical work has explored ovarian cancer metastasis models.
expanded.mechanismDetail: NNMT methylates nicotinamide (NAM) to 1-methylnicotinamide (MNA), consuming SAM and indirectly draining the NAD+ salvage pathway. By inhibiting NNMT at its substrate site, 5-Amino-1MQ raises intracellular NAM available for NAD+ resynthesis (NAMPT pathway), increases NAD+ and SAM, and lowers MNA. Functional consequences in adipocytes include suppressed lipogenesis, increased mitochondrial activity, and reduced adiposity in vivo. NNMT is overexpressed in obesity, T2D, several cancers, and aged muscle, providing the rationale for therapeutic inhibition.
expanded.safetyDetail: Safety data are limited to rodent studies, where 5-Amino-1MQ is reported as well-tolerated at the doses used (5-20 mg/kg) without overt adverse effects, weight loss beyond fat mass, or food-intake changes. No formal toxicology, genotoxicity, reproductive, or chronic-dosing studies are publicly available. As a quaternary ammonium small molecule, distribution and elimination in humans are uncharacterized. Vendor-grade material varies in purity; community use is unregulated.
